children: The Indian rupee opened higher on November 25, supported by a revival in foreign investor appetite for local equities and a mounting sense that the currency's outlook is turning more favourable.
The rupee opened higher by 18 paise at 92.73 per dollar, compared with Monday's close of 92.91.

According to Finrex, the Indian Rupee to open at 92.64 which is flat and is expected to remain in the range of 92.25 and 93.35 with expectations of RBI buying dollars to keep the rupee in the range and not very strong.

Dollar Index has moved lower from yesterday after it crossed 104 on Monday evening after the US PMI data which came stronger than expected. Brent Oil January Series had fallen to below $ 90 per barrel is now up to 90.68 this morning in the Asia trading.

Exporters got a chance to hedge their receivables on Monday when rupee fell to 93.05 on RBI buying $ while importers keep getting chances to hedge due to FPIs selling $ to buy Indian Assets, it added.

Asian currencies traded mixed against the US dollar, with the Chinese yuan emerging as the strongest performer, rising 0.31 percent, followed by the Taiwan dollar, which gained 0.13 percent, and the South Korean won, which edged up 0.08 percent. The Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar also posted marginal gains of 0.03 percent and 0.02 percent, respectively.

On the other hand, the Japanese yen was the worst performer, declining 0.19 percent, followed by the Philippine peso, which fell 0.16 percent, and the Indonesian rupiah, which slipped 0.09 percent. The Thai baht also edged lower by 0.04 percent.

The US dollar took a breather on Wednesday ahead of inflation and growth data, the last major readings before a December Federal Reserve policy meeting at which traders see a 97% chance of an interest rate hike.

The yen held steady following figures showing Japan's service-sector prices jumped to a 36-year high in October. The Australian dollar climbed after data showing hotter-than-forecast inflation in October.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against six peers, was flat at 103.85 following a 0.44% slide in the prior session. The euro was down 0.03% at $1.0961.
The yen edged 0.03% lower to 159.28 a dollar, while sterling weakened 0.05% to $1.3106.

title: Currency Check | Rupee opens 18 paise higher at 92.73/ dollar; Asian peers trade mixed
